sources.citation: Kramer, Raija. 2014. Die Sprache der Fali in Nordkamerun: Eine funktionale Beschreibung. (Grammatische Analysen Afrikanischer Sprachen 45.) Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. 344 pp. [publisher 'Blick ins Buch' preview, book pp. 1-78 = front matter, ch.1, all of ch.2 'Phonologische Skizze, Silben und Ton' (pp.31-64), start of ch.3]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.F26 K73 2014); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.F26 K73 2014
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (no Akzent/Betonung anywhere in pp.1-78; verified visually on pp.61,64). p.61: no lexical tonal oppositions; two register tones (H/L) with grammatical function on verbs. p.64: 'Prosodie ist kein Gegenstand dieser Arbeit' -- prosody explicitly excluded; lexeme tone patterns unpredictable and marked throughout. p.58: long vowels occur only in open first syllables of disyllables; vowel quantity non-distinctive.
blurb only: 'phonological outline considering also the syllable structure and tonal system'; no mention of stress

sources.note: The only dedicated phonological description of South Fali (Fali of Ram); a 61-page structuralist phonology of this series normally has a 'ton / accent' section and is the most likely place for an explicit stress/accent statement. Kramer 2014 relies on it for the phoneme inventory.
